CodeLima 0.3.1 fixes duplicate terminal tabs and other TUI actions caused by
handling a key's press, repeat, and release as separate commands.

- Tab opening/closing, focus and Info toggles, search, menu commands, and
  form/selector actions run once per reported key press.
- Choosing or cancelling a selector leaves its parent form open. Shortcut
  followups cannot submit that form or type into a newly exposed form or shell,
  including when the modifier is released first.
- Navigation and text editing retain held-key repeats without an extra step
  on release. Search and form paste retain their input behavior.

Upgrade an existing Homebrew installation:

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade codelima
codelima daemon update
codelima --version
```

Reopen attached TUIs after upgrading to use the corrected keyboard handling.
Legacy terminals that encode autorepeat as fresh presses cannot distinguish a
held key from separate presses.

**Qualification status:** local Linux arm64 automated checks and live host-TUI
checks pass. Publication requires native verification, race, integration, and
package tests on macOS arm64 and Linux amd64/arm64. Physical macOS keyboard,
actual Homebrew upgrade, Lima VM/forwarding, and the full interactive QA matrix
remain unverified, as does the previously deferred full upstream Ghostty Debug
suite. These limitations remain tracked in TODO #41/#43/#44/#45; this patch
does not mark them complete. See the
[qualification report](https://github.com/brianrackle/codelima/blob/main/plans/shortcut_release_qa.md).

Archives include both `codelima` and `codelima-renderer-worker`; keep them
together for manual installations. Supported targets are macOS arm64,
Linux amd64, and Linux arm64.
